answer: A history chain gives an identity its weight: each answer hashes to the previous one, so only a continuous record across epochs proves one operator did the work. One nebula counts as 1,000 linked hashes, and no weight accrues until the chain holds a full nebula; any 14-day gap drops the chain to its nadir of zero and forces a restart, and a willow of 90 days of unbroken history earns full weight. 100 fakes must each build a 90-day chain, so cloning costs 9,000 days of graded work.
